question: Malarial parasite shows which type of asexual reproduction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Multiple fission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Malarial parasite, Plasmodium, reproduces asexually through a process known as **multiple fission**.
 
• During multiple fission, the nucleus of the parasite divides multiple times before the cell splits into several daughter cells.
 
• This process allows for rapid multiplication of the parasite within the host's body.
 
• Multiple fission typically occurs in the liver cells and red blood cells of the infected host.
 
• It is a crucial part of the parasite's life cycle, contributing to the spread and severity of malaria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission**

 
 
• A type of asexual reproduction commonly found in prokaryotes like bacteria.
 
• Involves the division of a single organism into two equal parts, each with a copy of the DNA.
 
 
 
• **Regeneration**
 
 
• A process where organisms regrow lost or damaged parts.
 
• Commonly seen in species like starfish and planarians.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• A type of asexual reproduction seen in organisms like yeast and Hydra.
 
• Involves the formation of a new organism from a small projection growing on the parent organism.
